unusualness_rating: 2 (fairly standard). The design is a conventional aspiration-level spline logit with team and year fixed effects, familiar from the performance-feedback literature the paper cites. The unusual elements are contextual rather than methodological: the one-point-ahead aspiration definition and the removal of the final two minutes of each game (D01 PDF pages 9 and 16), both explicitly justified. Inference choices (no clustering, star key, marginal effects at means) are typical of the field at the time.

documentation_scores.specificity: 3. Variable definitions are specific for the dependent variable, the performance spline, the controls and the fixed effects (D01 PDF pages 8-9), and the software command is named. But the estimator variant (conditional vs. dummy fixed effects), the covariance type, the handling of penalty-nullified plays, kneel-downs and neutral sites, and the exact two-minute boundary are not stated.
documentation_scores.precision: 3. Odds ratios are printed to three decimals with standard errors, log-likelihoods to four decimals and marginal effects to four decimals with standard errors (D01 PDF pages 11-12), which supports close comparison. However, several standard errors round to 0.000, no exact p-values are given, and the marginal-effect computation (derivative vs. finite difference; treatment of the group effect; standard-error method) is not described, so Table 6 cannot be reproduced without assumptions.
documentation_scores.exhaustiveness: 2. Sample construction is documented in outline (seasons, regular season, overtime, last two minutes, counts before and after), but intermediate counts per exclusion are not given, missing-data handling is absent, the chi-square test of below-vs-above difference is unspecified, and the robustness analyses in endnote 4 and the quarters-remaining check (D01 PDF page 9) are reported without any numbers. No supplement or online appendix exists (publication_packet.json: supplements_included empty; search not found).

unavailable_source_fallbacks.item: Play-by-play source used by the authors (not named in the article)
unavailable_source_fallbacks.fallback: nflverse play-by-play built with nflfastR from NFL Game Center feeds (S1). Treat differences in play parsing (play_type coding of penalties, fakes, aborted plays) as a vintage/provider difference and report sample counts at each step.
unavailable_source_fallbacks.vintage_issue: Provider parse may classify some plays differently from the authors' source; the authors' original counts cannot be matched exactly if their source included or excluded penalty-nullified plays differently.
